chapter: Brass bands, union and theatre work
title: The theatre band at the Palace under Howard
summary: Barnes played show tunes by ear in the Palace theatre band led by trumpeter Howard, with Paul in the group.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Maybe another thing we didn't get to is when you played at the, this theatre, why don't you have some kind of a theatre band in the 30s? Oh, yeah, I played at the Palace.
Who was the leader of that band?
The Palace, let's see, Howard. Howard was the leader. Yeah. Now what kind of a job was that?
Did they have movies or a show, like a stage show?
All of them. All of them. And you were the band that would stay there whenever the show came through? That's right. You were the company. Was that alright? Did you have to read music for that job?

Well, no, we can pick them up. We know the show tunes. We know all the show tunes. You play the show tunes? Pick up from the cuts and all. What kind of show tunes? Well, everything. You know, like they come out with a fast dance or talking or something or laughing. You know, you work with me just work like that.
How big a band was that?
That was a pretty good band. Paul was in the band. Paul was in the band. Yeah. Sisyphoon, carlet, trumpet, trombone, bass, violin, drums. He had a good band. Just one trumpet? Yeah. Just Howard.
Mm-hmm. How was Howard playing then? How was Howard playing then? Howard was first Howard.
He was playing first Howard. He was getting out of here.
